title: S8_TEN
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were isolated from EDTA anticoagulated venous blood of SCADR patients and healthy volunteers after ficoll gradient sorting using 15 ml tubes (Corning) and resuspended in 1ml of ice-cold PBS containing 1% BSA and 0.25mM EDTA prior to FACS sorting of propidium negative (PI) cells using a Beckman Coulter MoFlo Astrios for dead cell removal. Sorted cells were immediately processed for scRNA-seq analysis. Skin biopsies were processed essentially as previously described by Kim D et al. (Nat Med. 2020;26(2):236-243. doi:10.1038/s41591-019-0733-7) with minor modifications. Skin isolated cells were not ACK treated after 40-μm cell strainers filtration and were resuspended in 0.5 ml ice-cold PBS containing 1% BSA and 0.25mM EDTA prior to cell sorting. Alive cells were isolated with Beckman Coulter MoFlo Astrios after PI and Hoecht staining and immediately processed for scRNA-seq analysis. After isolation, the cells were diluted at a concentration of 500-1000 cells/ml in PBS 2% FCS and checked for viability and absence of significant doublets or aggregates.

The cells were then loaded into a Chromium Single Cell Controller (10x Genomics, Pleasanton, CA) in a NextGEM chip G together with beads, master mix reagents (containing RT enzyme and poly-dt RT primers), and oil to generate single-cell-containing droplets. Single-cell Gene Expression libraries were then prepared using Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 3’ Kit v3.1 following the manufacturer’s instructions. Quality control was performed with a TapeStation 4200 (Agilent) and QuBit dsDNA high sensitivity assay (Thermo) following manufacturer instructions. With this procedure, the cDNAs from distinct droplets harbor a distinct and unique 10x “cell barcode”.
data_processing: Cell Ranger (v7.0.1, 10x Genomics) was used to align reads to the human reference genome (hg19)
